subject: Data incident: suspected token exfiltration - coordination and evidence handoff
messages:
From: Finex Security <security@finexcorp.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-09T23:42:00Z
Subject: Data incident: suspected token exfiltration - initial alert

Hi Monica / Laura / Rishi,

We detected anomalous outbound activity from our Redwood tenant (customer: FinexCorp) at ~2027-04-09T22:58:00Z. Initial triage by our SecOps team indicates a small set of service tokens were posted to an external repo for a short window. We believe the tokens granted read-only access to metrics and usage logs, but we are still validating scope.

What we need from Redwood immediately:
- Confirmation of the DPA notification process and the exact clause/clock start you use for "notification to controller". Our legal wants a timestamp.
- Contact for Redwood forensics (name + mobile) to coordinate live evidence transfer.
- Whether any Redwood subprocessors (e.g., cloud provider, logging vendor) need to be engaged and the process for cross-subprocessor evidence requests.
- A secure location to upload forensic artifacts. We have prepared a bucket: https://s3.amazonaws.com/finexcorp-logs/incident-20270409/ (read-only link for now).

Attached is a short CSV with the alert summary (finex_alert_summary.csv).

We appreciate an acknowledgement within your DPA timelines. Please advise next steps; our DPO (dpo@finexcorp.com) is copied.

Thanks,
Samir Patel
Head of Security, FinexCorp
security@finexcorp.com

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Finex Security <security@finexcorp.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-10T01:08:00Z
Subject: Re: Data incident: suspected token exfiltration - initial alert

Samir — thanks for the alert and the S3 link; we have received the CSV. A quick acknowledgement while we assemble our incident team:

- Acknowledge receipt: Redwood confirms receipt of the alert at 2027-04-10T01:08:00Z (UTC).
- Forensics contact: Monica Patel (Incident Lead) — +1-415-555-0123, monica_patel@redwood.com.
- We will need to validate the token scope. Please confirm the token IDs in the CSV map to customer-facing service tokens or internal build keys.

Regarding the DPA: our standard DPA (Section 5, Notification) requires "notification without undue delay and, where feasible, within 72 hours" for controller-level notification when personal data is impacted. However, we treat high-confidence exfiltration as actionable immediately and will aim to provide:
  * An initial acknowledgement within 24 hours (we're doing that now),
  * A preliminary incident report within 72 hours with scope and remediation actions, and
  * A final detailed report as the investigation completes.

For subprocessors: please identify any third-party partners (CloudOps, logging vendor) that touched the affected tokens. We will need a list and their contact points to request logs and to execute any DPA subprocessor cooperation clauses. Note that where cross-border transfers are involved we may need to reference SCCs or rely on our existing transfer mechanisms — please flag any EU data subjects in the affected datasets.

Next practical steps:
1) Finex to attach the raw alert logs and a mapping of token IDs -> service names to the S3 folder.
2) Finex to confirm whether the tokens were used to access personal data (even indirectly).
3) Redwood will engage our cloud subprocessor contact and share a minimal evidence request list (hashes, timestamps, request URIs).
4) Legal (Rishi) to follow up on DPA clause text and any additional contractual obligations.

We will treat evidence uploads as confidential. If you prefer, we can provide a short evidence transfer access form to sign before we pull logs from the bucket.

—Monica
Monica Patel
Head of Customer Reliability (Incident Response)
Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Finex Security <security@finexcorp.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-10T06:21:00Z
Subject: Re: Data incident: suspected token exfiltration - initial alert

Monica / Samir — thanks for the quick handoff. A few legal points and an evidence checklist to keep the DPA obligations clear: 

1) Acknowledgement & timelines
   - We confirm the 24-hour acknowledgement (this thread). Per our DPA Section 5 and applicable EU data protection rules, the controller (Finex) and Redwood as subprocessors must cooperate; the operational clock for "notification to controller" is triggered by confirmed personal data exposure. If it remains unclear whether personal data was accessed, we will treat this as a potential breach and follow the cooperative timeline: preliminary report within 72 hours, fuller report as investigations conclude.

2) Scope & evidence to request from Finex (preliminary):
   - Alerting events with timestamps (UTC) and token IDs (exact strings).
   - Resource access logs (request path, user-agent, source IPs) for the affected tokens for +/- 2 hours around alert windows.
   - Any sampled payloads or request bodies that indicate personal data access (redact PII when sharing; if impossible, we will arrange a secure NDA-backed channel).

3) Subprocessors and cross-border transfer
   - If Finex uses a separate vendor (ops-admin@cloudvendor.io) to manage buckets or logging, we will need to issue a subprocessor evidence request to that vendor. Redwood's DPA allows us to request reasonable assistance from subprocessors but may require Finex's authorization when Finex is the controller; please identify subprocessors so we can triage.

4) Technical notes
   - Encryption-in-transit or at-rest does not eliminate the need to investigate. If keys were exfiltrated, treat as a full compromise. If the tokens only permitted read-only metrics and no PII, we will still document the event but the notification scope may be narrower.

I attached a short internal checklist (Rishi_incident_checklist.pdf) describing evidence types we will request. For any evidence that contains PII, we'll request a controlled sharing mechanism (Drive folder with DLP + expiration) and limited access.

Please add any missing items; Monica, please confirm who on Redwood will be the technical on-call for log pulls so Finex knows who to grant access.

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Contracts
Redwood Inference

From: Finex Security <security@finexcorp.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: DPO Finex <dpo@finexcorp.com>, Ops Admin <ops-admin@cloudvendor.io>
Date: 2027-04-10T14:37:00Z
Subject: Re: Data incident: suspected token exfiltration - initial alert

Monica / Rishi — appreciate the fast response and the checklist. Quick updates: 

- We uploaded the raw alert bundles and request traces to the S3 folder (https://s3.amazonaws.com/finexcorp-logs/incident-20270409/). Files are: alert_bundle_20270409.tar.gz (redacted), request_traces_20270409.ndjson, finex_alert_summary.csv.
- Token mapping: tokens.csv in the bucket maps the token IDs to service names. Early look: tokens were used to pull metrics only; we have not found payloads containing obvious PII, but analysis is ongoing.
- Subprocessor: Ops Admin (ops-admin@cloudvendor.io) manages the bucket and will coordinate any additional log exports. They are on this thread.

Next steps we propose:
1) Redwood to provide the forensic contact (ok — Monica + on-call engineer).
2) Ops Admin to grant a short-lived read role to monica_patel@redwood.com and laura_bennett@redwood.com for the incident bucket; please confirm when access is granted.
3) If Redwood requires a signed evidence-sharing form, we can accept a PDF and return a countersigned copy; otherwise the bucket will be our working medium.

We will prioritize any artifacts indicating PII access and notify Finex legal (copied).

—Samir
Samir Patel
Head of Security, FinexCorp
security@finexcorp.com
